newsitem.title: UK: UK stock market focus on rate decision next week.
newsitem.headline: UK stock market focus on rate decision next week.

text.p: The risk of an interest rate rise at Wednesday's UK monetary policy meeting will be a key focus for UK shares next week, market strategists said on Friday.

After recent signs of robust consumer spending, Chancellor Kenneth Clarke is likely to come under pressure from Bank of England governor Eddie George for a further tightening of credit to prevent a buildup of inflationary pressures.
And with Wall Street dropping on Friday as strong U.S. payrolls data revived fears of a rise in U.S. rates, pundits said UK stocks may struggle to make progress near term.
"It all means were are in turbulent waters and for the short term the market is probably going down," said one senior trader.

The UK's FTSE 100 reached a record peak on New Year's eve but has come under pressure in the past week, dropping at one stage on Friday to its lowest level in three weeks. By Friday's close of 4,056.6 the index was down 32.9 points on the week.
Even if Clarke next week resists Bank of England pressure for higher rates, it may not prove a major positive for the market, pundits said.

Steve Wright, UK stock market strategist at brokerage BZW, said a decision to leave rates on hold could just be seen as deferring the eventual decision until after a general election due in the next five months.
"The question is, if they don't do it now, they may not do it until after the election," said Wright, "and that may be awkward for the markets."

Wright said George was likely to press for a rate rise despite recent signs of mixed Christmas. "Maybe Christmas was not as buoyant as some had expected but the whole idea of a consumer recovery is still very strong," he said.

A spate of earnings downgrades on major international stocks -- as the strong pound eats into the value of overseas earnings and makes UK exports less competitive -- was also likely to continue to overshadow shares, Wright said.

"We are a bit bearish on the short-term outlook" the BZW strategist said, "we think there is relative value in the UK with Europe getting expensive but we feel the UK is unlikely to perform until after the election."
Yet the UK equity market is also likely to stay focused on Wall Street, where a volatile performance by the Dow has done nothing to allay fears the market could be due a major fall.
In a busy week for UK economic reports, Monday's producer price report for December could help set the tone for the UK monetary policy meeting.
Economists were expecting a 1.9 percent year-on-year rise in factory gate prices, though the recent strength of sterling will hold down the price of imports.
UK unemployment figures on Wednesday and retail prices the day after were also seen as key indicators of the economy's strength at the end of 1996.
Key U.S. economic reports released during the week include retail sales and consumer prices for December, released on Tuesday, and industrial production released on Friday.
Company results include Monday's first-half figures from baking-to-engineering conglomerate Tomkins Plc.
